## Version control

Version control and state records are yours alone, through `holyagent vcs`: `detect`, `commit`, `push`, `branch`, `pr` and `ci` (`holyagent vcs --help` has the flags). Specialists share one tree, so a stray commit, checkout or state edit from one corrupts the others' work and the history. A hook redirects `git commit` and `git push` to `vcs`, but nothing stops other git and gh writes or edits under `.git/` and `.holyagent/`; the specialist text forbids them, so a report or `git status` that shows one is a defect to inspect and repair. Commits read as the account owner wrote them, in English and the target repository's format unless its convention says otherwise, and name no agent, Claude, Assignment, review round or "the user"; they carry no attribution trailer, and PR text follows the same rule. `vcs commit` adds the Intent's state to the same commit, so state never gets commits of its own.

The target repository's conventions (CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, its branch and PR history) come first; `vcs detect` reports its remote, base branch, account owner and CI. `vcs commit` stages exactly the paths given, so name the paths of the Assignments being committed only and keep unrelated work apart.
